title: Generic-field and affine-chart models of meromorphic sections on a regular space
statement:
Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian separated algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]: regular means all etale scheme charts are regular; Noetherian means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian; separated means the diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion. Let $\mathcal K_X$ be the sheafification on the small etale site of $U\mapsto S(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$, where $S(U)$ consists of functions whose multiplication on $\mathcal O_U$ is injective. For a line module $L$, put $\mathcal K_X(L)=L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal K_X$.

The space $X$ is reduced (its etale scheme charts have no nonzero nilpotents in their local rings) and normal (the local rings of those charts are domains integrally closed in their fraction fields). Every Noetherian etale scheme chart is a finite disjoint union of integral regular normal schemes; in particular the rings of nonempty connected affine charts are Noetherian normal domains. The irreducible components of $X$ have finitely many generic points $\eta$, all contained in its schematic locus; their local rings $k(\eta)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ are fields. With $j_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}k(\eta)\to X$, there are natural identifications
$$\mathcal K_X=\prod_\eta j_{\eta,*}k(\eta),\qquad \mathcal K_X(L)=\prod_\eta j_{\eta,*}L_\eta,$$
and hence $\Gamma(X,\mathcal K_X(L))=\prod_\eta L_\eta$, where $L_\eta$ is a one-dimensional $k(\eta)$-vector space. The natural maps $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K_X$ and $L\to\mathcal K_X(L)$ are injective. For every dense open $W\subset X$, restriction induces an isomorphism on global meromorphic sections of $L$ and an injection $\Gamma(X,L)\to\Gamma(W,L|_W)$.

For every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, $\mathcal K_X(U)=Q(A)$, the localization of $A$ at its non-zero-divisors. Restricting $\mathcal K_X$ and $\mathcal K_X(L)$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ gives the usual scheme meromorphic sheaves, via the ordinary-to-etale module comparison [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison]; these identifications commute with further etale restrictions.

proof.text: Every etale scheme chart is regular by hypothesis. Clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] makes all its local rings integrally closed domains, so they have no nonzero nilpotents; this proves normality and reducedness of $X$ in the stated chart sense. On a Noetherian chart clause (2) gives finitely many disjoint clopen normal integral components. Their local rings are the original regular local rings, so the components are regular too. A nonempty connected affine chart has just one component. Its ring $A$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme], is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and is integrally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal], using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] to identify all its localizations with normal local rings. The empty chart instead has zero ring.

By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-topology] and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components], $|X|$ has finitely many irreducible components. Sobriety [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] supplies their unique generic points. Choose a dense open scheme $V\subset X$ by [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-dense-scheme-open]. Every generic point $\eta_i$ lies in $V$: remove the other finitely many components from its component, giving a nonempty open subset of $X$; density makes $V$ meet this subset, and an open meeting an irreducible component contains its generic point. Thus all $\eta_i$ lie in the schematic locus. Every open of a Noetherian topological space is quasi-compact: a cover without a finite subcover would produce a strictly increasing infinite sequence of finite unions of its members, contrary to the descending condition on their closed complements. Thus $V$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, hence Noetherian. Each $\eta_i$ is a generic point of an integral normal component of this regular Noetherian scheme $V$, by clauses (1) and (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal]. Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] there to see that $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$ is a field, and [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] after [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] to see that $L_{\eta_i}$ has dimension one.

For an etale scheme chart $a:U\to X$, a point $u$ is a generic point of a component of $U$ exactly when $a(u)$ is one of the $\eta_i$. Indeed a generic $u$ cannot have image with a strict generalization: [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-etale-specializations] would lift it to a strict generalization of $u$. Conversely, a generalization of a point over $\eta_i$ must still map to $\eta_i$, since $\eta_i$ has no strict generalization; the noncollapse clause of that same node makes it equal to $u$. In a scheme, points with no strict generalizations are precisely generic points of components. Use the open scheme $V$ of step 2 near $\eta_i$. The fibre $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k(\eta_i)$ is the fibre of the etale scheme map $U\times_XV\to V$. By [lem-sfb-local-spectrum-base-change-stalks] its local rings at points over $\eta_i$ are $\mathcal O_{U,u}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] it is a disjoint union of spectra of these fields. For affine $U$ there are finitely many such $u$, by step 1. This identifies the generic fibre, including its structure maps, with the finite disjoint union of the generic local spectra of $U$.

proof.text: For every affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A$ is reduced and Noetherian by step 1 and [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Give it the ordinary quasi-coherent sheaf $\widetilde{Q(A)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and pass to the etale site using [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Every map $f:W\to U$ between etale charts is etale: factor it as its graph $W\to W\times_XU$ and the projection to $U$. The graph is a section of the etale projection to $W$; it is an open immersion since it is a base change of the open diagonal of that etale map, using [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Etale base change is [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and the scheme composition and open-immersion assertions are [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. For an affine chart map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] and [lem-sfb-etale-total-fraction-base-change] identify its pullback with $\widetilde{Q(B)}$. The comparison sends $(a/s)\otimes b$ to $f(a)b/f(s)$; applying two chart maps gives the same fraction as their composite, so the identity and cocycle conditions hold. Affine opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; gluing over them gives these modules on arbitrary charts. Now [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-cartesian-chart-family] gives a quasi-coherent module $F$ on $X$ with $F(U)=Q(A)$ and the specified fraction restrictions. Multiplication and unit glue too, since those fraction comparisons are algebra maps.

The fraction presheaf defining $\mathcal K_X$ maps to $F$: a denominator regular on a chart is regular on each affine open, where it is a non-zero-divisor. These local fraction maps glue. On an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, regularity of multiplication on $\mathcal O_U$ is equivalent to being a non-zero-divisor in $A$: one implication follows on global sections and the other by localization on affine basic opens. When $\mathcal O_U$ is read as the etale structure sheaf of [def-trf-algebraic-space] restricted to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, injectivity on every affine etale $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$ is the first clause $f(T_A)\subseteq T_B$ of [lem-sfb-etale-total-fraction-base-change], so both readings give exactly the non-zero-divisors of $A$. Thus the presheaf map on affine objects is exactly $S(U)^{-1}A=Q(A)=F(U)$. Every chart and every covering refines to affine charts. Consequently any section of $F$ locally comes from a fraction, and two fractions with the same image agree after such a refinement. This proves that $F$ has the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], hence $F=\mathcal K_X$. In particular $\mathcal K_X(U)=Q(A)$ canonically, and it is quasi-coherent. On a scheme chart its Zariski restriction is the ordinary meromorphic sheaf [def-sc-meromorphic-module]: both sheafifications are the same fractions on affine opens. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] therefore identifies its etale restriction with that ordinary sheaf's etale realization. Tensoring with the line module, locally free of rank one, gives the same comparison for $\mathcal K_X(L)$ using [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison]. All comparisons keep $a/s$ and local line generators, so they commute with further etale restrictions.

Put $G=\prod_i j_{\eta_i,*}k(\eta_i)$. Its restriction to a chart is the pushforward from the generic fibres, by [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. On affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, step 3 therefore identifies $G(U)$ with $\prod_{u\text{ generic in }U}\mathcal O_{U,u}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the canonical map $Q(A)\to G(U)$ is an isomorphism: its components are exactly the localization maps at the minimal primes, corresponding to the components by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. These maps are restrictions of a single sheaf map: send a local fraction to its pullback on each generic fibre. Its denominators are units there, since a regular function remains nonzero at every generic point of a reduced chart; this also follows from the total-quotient decomposition just cited. Thus $\mathcal K_X\to G$ is an isomorphism on the affine basis and hence on the site. To twist, trivialize $L$ on an etale cover. On a frame $e$, tensoring sends a tuple $(a_i)$ to $(a_i e_{\eta_i})$; changing frame by a unit $v$ multiplies both expressions by $v_{\eta_i}$. These maps glue and prove $\mathcal K_X(L)=\prod_i j_{\eta_i,*}L_{\eta_i}$. Evaluating at $X$ gives $\Gamma(X,\mathcal K_X(L))=\prod_i L_{\eta_i}$ by the definition of direct image.

proof.text: On an affine chart $A\to Q(A)$ is injective: $a/1=0$ says $sa=0$ for a non-zero-divisor $s$, hence $a=0$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. It follows that $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K_X$ is injective, since equality of sheaf sections is local. On a local frame of $L$ its map to $\mathcal K_X(L)$ is this same injection, so it too is injective. Let $W\subseteq X$ be dense open. The finite-component argument of step 2 puts every $\eta_i$ in $W$. Restricting the product sheaves of step 6 to $W$ leaves exactly the same generic fields and fibres. Their global sections on $W$ and $X$ are therefore the identical product, and restriction is its identity. If a section of $L$ restricts to zero on $W$, its image in this product is zero and the just-proved injection forces the original section to be zero. This proves both dense-open claims.

tool_uses.why: Normality of regular schemes and finite clopen normal integral components of a normal Noetherian scheme; used on charts, not to replace the unit route.
Noetherian coordinate rings on affine opens of locally Noetherian schemes; needed on etale charts.
A domain whose prime localizations are integrally closed is integrally closed; used only for a connected affine chart.
Identifies affine scheme local rings with prime localizations for chart and generic-fibre calculations.
Finiteness of irreducible components of a Noetherian topological space; the unit has no substitute topology lemma.
Identifies the generic local ring of an integral scheme with its fraction field, applied in the dense open scheme.
A line module on an integral scheme has one-dimensional generic stalk, applied to each dense-open component.
Compares ordinary and etale line modules on schemes and their pullbacks; needed for the chart comparison and generic fibres.
An etale scheme over a field is a disjoint union of separable field spectra; used to evaluate generic-fibre sections.
The affine quasi-coherent sheaf associated with a module has that module as its global sections.
The ordinary/etale equivalence for quasi-coherent modules transfers the affine fraction module to chart sites.
Affine pullback of associated module sheaves is tensor product, needed with the new fraction base-change lemma.
Affine opens form a scheme basis, allowing the explicit chart modules to glue on all charts.
Restricts etale direct image to a chart by the fibre product, exactly the generic-fibre computation.
The total quotient ring of a reduced Noetherian ring is the product of its minimal-prime localizations; used for chart sections.
Identifies irreducible components of an affine spectrum with minimal primes; needed to index the fraction product.
Etale base change for space charts, used for projections in the graph argument.
Open immersions and composites of etale scheme maps are etale, used for maps of charts.
